title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction
abstract: arXiv:2610.12299v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Egocentric world models predict first-person observations conditioned on an agent's actions, but most focus on a single agent. Real embodied settings often involve multiple agents that act and interact within a shared environment. Existing multi-agent world models rely on coarse actions like locomotion, camera control, or discrete commands, leaving fine-grained embodied interactions underexplored. We formulate multi-agent egocentric world modeling as synchronized ego-stream generation for multiple agents interacting through fine-grained actions in a shared world. This requires cross-view action consistency, shared-environment consistency, and consistent propagation of interaction-induced state updates. We propose Multi-agent Egocentric World Model (ME-World), which jointly denoises multiple ego streams in a shared token sequence, conditions each stream on all agents' target-view poses, and grounds generation with shared environment mem

translated_title: 具有细粒度具身交互的多智能体第一人称世界模型
translated_abstract: 第一人称（自我中心）世界模型以智能体的动作为条件来预测第一人称观测，但现有研究大多聚焦于单一智能体。而真实的具身场景中往往涉及多个智能体在共享环境中行动并相互交互。现有的多智能体世界模型依赖于移动、相机控制或离散指令等粗粒度动作，对细粒度的具身交互探索不足。我们将多智能体第一人称世界建模形式化为：多个智能体在共享世界中通过细粒度动作进行交互时的同步第一人称视频流生成。这需要满足跨视角动作一致性、共享环境一致性，以及交互引起的状态更新的一致传播。我们提出了多智能体第一人称世界模型（ME-World），它在共享的 token 序列中对多个第一人称视频流进行联合去噪，将每个视频流条件于所有智能体的目标视角位姿，并以共享环境记忆为基础来引导生成（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出首个面向细粒度具身交互的多智能体第一人称世界模型 ME-World，通过在共享 token 序列中联合去噪多个第一人称视频流、以所有智能体的目标视角位姿为条件，并借助共享环境记忆，实现了多智能体交互中的跨视角一致性、共享环境一致性以及交互状态更新的一致传播。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ME-World, a multi-agent egocentric world model enabling fine-grained embodied interactions among multiple agents in a shared environment by jointly denoising multiple ego streams in a shared token sequence, conditioning each stream on all agents' target-view poses, and grounding generation with a shared environment memory to ensure cross-view consistency, shared-environment consistency, and consistent propagation of interaction-induced state updates.
